mission.title: Killjoy
mission.description: Find Raini and learn what the Elements are up to with the Blackwoods in Mara.

npc.say: Come see me at Club Paradise in Hampton Green some day, sugar; I'll be sure to make it worth your while. I know what the Merv pays you.
A little resistance isn't always a bad thing.
I think she's warming up to us.
Raini just can't get enough of ol' Effy. And who can blame her?

There is more to this plot than the petty ambitions of Mercury and Thallia; neither of them would be able, much less want, to hatch a scheme requiring the cooperation of their fellow Elements. There must be some specific reason, and some steadier hand, behind these "distractions" in Mara.
There's something to be said for simply slitting someone's throat.

phase.briefing:
I've seen enough to believe that Raini has begun taking her "bad girl" image far too seriously. This recent spate of disobedience by the other Elements has pointed to her in several ways. It's time to rein her in.
Go to Apollyon and find her.

enter.say: That's a known hangout for Raini's "5 Points" gang. I'm reading an active terminal in there, so get to it and we'll see if we can track her across her network.

done.say:
What? Her operating system is so old that our network hack won't even run! Damn, I can't stand people who don't keep their software up to date!
Looks like we're going to have to go to plan B. Um, maybe Flood will have one of those for once.

phase.briefing:
For the love of--
I can't waste time with these bastions of ineptitude. Fine. I'm going to have to crack open the expense account for this one, and if the Merovingian doesn't like it, he has only his own cavalier attitude toward women to blame.
Nicky G. has been summoned. You're going to talk to her so that I don't have to. She'll know where to find Raini.

enter.say: Whoa, Nicky G. doesn't slink out of her ritzy room in Paradise Lost for chump change. Flood must have shelled out a pretty penny. Scuttlebutt has it that she and the Merv used to know each other... But then again, they say a lot about both of them, so who knows?

talk.say: Raini? That kid? She's strictly low-class, but yeah, I know some people she parties with. I'll make a few calls. Your operator will have the information in a jiff.

done.say: I guess it pays to know people, huh? I wonder what other numbers she's got in her little black book.

phase.briefing:
Say what you like about Nicky G.; she is, at least, professional, unlike most of the people with whom I am forced to deal. Little wonder that she left the Merovingian's employ...
Ah, and then there's you, {player}. Go see Raini. She'd better have a good explanation for her recent underhanded dealings with Mercury. Not that I expect her to.
Oh, and I'm sending the Twins along, just to make sure that her 5 Points don't delay you.

enter.say: I'm reading a bunch of Exile programs in there; a couple of them look like our Twins.

done.say: You treat us right, we'll treat you right.
If she continues to be obstinate, tell her that we will send in the Effectuator.
A little resistance isn't always a bad thing.
I think she's warming up to us.

objective.text: Tell Raini that Flood will send in the Effectuator

talk.say:
Hey, what's the big idea? You can call off your goon squad here.
Mercury? Ha-ha! I am so over him. If he's geeking out on me again--
H-huh? No, no need for him! Uh, look, so you're saying Mercury and Thallia didn't tell you? They've been running distractions with the Blackwoods in Mara. Why? How should I know? Geez...

done.say: An interesting story...but I'm sure she isn't telling us everything. We'll follow that up, but I'm calling the Effectuator to keep her busy. This is one call that nincompoop won't pretend to miss...

Raini! Baby! Where've you been? I've looked all over! Well, never mind; we've got a lot of catching up to do! Did I tell you about that time with the helicopter inside Hel Club? Well, that wasn't even me, but the best part was that I...
Aw, crap! Do you know how long it took me to get rid of him last time?
Raini just can't get enough of ol' Effy. And who can blame her?

complete.say: And we were getting on so beautifully.

phase.briefing:
This is getting ridiculous, {player}. Now I'm to believe that Mercury and Thallia, whom we have already confronted, are up to something with the Blackwoods in Mara? All I can say that I truly believe at this point is that none of the Elements has been entirely truthful with us. If it wasn't such a bother, I'd say that we should have the whole lot of them recycled...
But before that, we'll have to look into this Blackwood thing. Or rather, you and Malphas will.

enter.say: Whenever Malphas shows up, you know that someone is in for it.

talk.say:
In general, the Mara Blackwoods are thought to be independent. However, as they are in a nearly constant state of poverty, they do not hesitate to retail their services to the highest bidder--and in their case the bidding does not usually go very high.
It seems to me that an interrogation of Mara Blackwoods is in order; I have found that when dealing with beings of such low understanding, pain and fear elicit the most honest response. They should not be overly difficult to break.

done.say: I don't think I'd like to be a Blackwood in Mara about now.

near.say: There's something to be said for simply slitting someone's throat.
There's something to be said for simply slitting someone's throat.

mission.finish: Well, that's Malphas' problem, isn't it? I have better things to do than to waste my time trying to extract anything useful from Blackwoods.
